mechanism: Build two pools (~227 SMA periods each) of High-based and Low-based moving averages; for each MA compute mean historical deviation of ZigZag peaks (or troughs) from that MA; shift MA by that mean to form envelope bands; at the zero bar take the cross-section of the upper (peak) and lower (trough) envelope surfaces and use min/mean/max of the cross-section as candidate current and next ZigZag node prices.
data_needed: OHLC history (depth_stories bars), ZigZag extrema with amplitude threshold, pool of iMA(PRICE_HIGH) and iMA(PRICE_LOW) handles from period START_MA onward, sums of ZZ-node deviations per MA.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Chart symbol NULL (any attached symbol); any timeframe; defaults depth_stories=5000 bars, amplitude=100 points; author recommends watching across timeframes/amplitudes.
why_new_for_mis: Turns a classical ZigZag into a multi-scale envelope-surface sensor that outputs predicted swing levels (price coordinate) from a statistical pool rather than a single fixed-deviation channel.
quote: We will need the following cross-section characteristics: maximum and minimum point, as well as the center of gravity of the cross-section (the arithmetic mean of all point values).

mechanism: Visualize/measure the short-period end of the envelope-pool cross-section ('comet tail'); the tail points with price, and the more it bends opposite to the prevailing move, the higher the chance of a trend change—a geometric regime-change cue from multi-MA envelope geometry.
data_needed: Same envelope-pool cross-section points ordered by averaging period; short-period subset orientation vs current price direction.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any symbol/timeframe with ZigZag amplitude in points; author stresses multi-TF observation.
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a geometric early trend-reversal sensor from multi-scale MA envelope curvature, not from lagging crossover or single oscillator.
quote: The comet's tail bends in the most intricate ways and the more it is turned in the opposite direction, the bigger the chance to see the trend change.

mechanism: Project cross-section max, min, and center-of-gravity onto the current bar as support/resistance levels; when the CoG point leads ahead of the rest of the peak cross-section, treat that as an upward-trend regime cue (and symmetrically for troughs).
data_needed: Per-bar maxH/minH/sumH/NUMBER_MA and maxL/minL/sumL/NUMBER_MA from the envelope pools; ZigZag last-node type (peak vs trough).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any attached chart symbol/TF; ZigZag amplitude in points.
why_new_for_mis: Derives live S/R and a directional regime flag from the statistics of an envelope surface cut, complementary to classical pivot or fractal S/R.
quote: When the points of the center of gravity of the cross-section get ahead of it (as the peaks in Fig. 9), this is an indication of the presence of the upward trend.
